--- gd-head-tags: - >- ``{=html} open-graph: title: >- [Graph.random_reference()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | EdgeCase description: >- Build a random reference graph with the same degrees (degree-preserving rewiring). twitter-card: title: >- [Graph.random_reference()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | EdgeCase description: >- Build a random reference graph with the same degrees (degree-preserving rewiring). title: >- [Graph.random_reference()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 bread-crumbs: false toc-depth: 3 description-meta: >- Build a random reference graph with the same degrees (degree-preserving rewiring). page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Build a random reference graph with the same degrees (degree-preserving rewiring). ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L41507-L41620){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-function} ```pythonsignature Graph.random_reference( iterations=1, connectivity=True, seed=None, ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![Random reference graph](../assets/graphs/random-reference.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="Left: an eight-node ring with four chords that close four triangles, average clustering 0.667. Right: random_reference(seed=8) rewires it with degree-preserving swaps: the four accent edges on the left are replaced by the four accent edges on the right, every node keeps its degree (4 or 2), and the triangles mostly disappear, leaving an average clustering of 0.229." width="100%"} The result keeps every node's degree but scrambles the wiring with random double edge swaps (`a-b, c-d` becomes `a-d, c-b`), destroying structure such as clustering and communities. Comparing a network with such references tells whether a property (high clustering, short paths, motifs) is more than a consequence of the degree sequence. It is the random baseline of `small_world_sigma()` and `small_world_omega()`. The graph is treated as undirected and simple (parallel edges and self-loops are dropped). With `connectivity=True`, swaps that would disconnect the graph are undone. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [iterations]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[1]{.dv}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Rewiring rounds, each attempting one swap per edge (default 1). [connectivity]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[True]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : If `True` (default), keep the graph connected. [seed]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Random seed for reproducible results. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [Graph]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : A new undirected, unweighted graph with the same nodes (IDs, labels and attributes kept) and rewired edges. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If the graph is directed or has fewer than four nodes or two edges. ::: ## Technical Notes {.doc-technical-notes} Follows NetworkX's `random_reference` (Maslov and Sneppen, 2002): endpoints are drawn with probability proportional to degree, then a random neighbor of each; the swap is applied when the four nodes are distinct and the new edges do not exist, and undone if it disconnects the first pair. Each round makes up to $2E/(V-1)$ attempts per edge. ## See Also {.doc-see-also} [](`~lattice_reference`) : A lattice-like graph with the same degrees. [](`~small_world_sigma`) : Compare clustering and path length with random references. [](`~average_clustering_coefficient`) : The mean clustering over all nodes. ## Examples {.doc-examples} Rewiring keeps every node's degree: ::: {#6af74b61 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ec.Graph().add_smallworld_graph(n=30, k=4, p=0.1, seed=1) reference = graph.random_reference(seed=2) def degrees(g): return sorted(g.get_degree(n) for n in g.get_node_ids()) degrees(graph) == degrees(reference), reference.is_connected() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` (True, True) ``` ::: ::: ### A club without its factions `karate_club()` links the 34 members of a university karate club who met outside the club, before it split in two. In a random graph with the same degrees, the members keep their number of friends and their `faction`, but the friendships no longer follow the factions. Only 10 of the 78 friendships crossed between them, and in the reference 36 do: ::: {#f0c55f9d .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} karate = ec.karate_club() reference = karate.random_reference(seed=1) def crossing(g): faction = dict(zip(g.get_node_df()["id"], g.get_node_df()["faction"])) return sum( faction[e.source] != faction[e.target] for e in map(g.get_edge, g.get_edge_ids()) ) crossing(karate), crossing(reference) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` (10, 36) ``` ::: ::: Its clustering falls from 0.57 to 0.29 as well. Whatever a property's value in the references, the degrees alone account for it: ::: {layout-ncol="2"} ::: {#ab946796 .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} karate.layout_kamada_kawai().plot( layout="pos", color_by="faction", label_by="label", width=320, height=360, legend=False, ) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ```{=html}
